title: Hard sets beat junk volume past ~20 / muscle
summary: A 2024 meta-regression on weekly set volume found hypertrophy returns flatten sharply above roughly 20 hard sets per muscle per week for trained lifters. Quality > stacking extras.
source: Simulated Habit Lab brief · volume meta-regression 2024

proposedChange.from: 20 hard sets / muscle / week soft cap
proposedChange.to: Keep the 20-set soft cap; prefer adding proximity-to-failure over a 5th accessory
proposedChange.explanation: If a muscle is already near 18–20 hard sets, we'll protect recovery instead of adding another isolation move.

title: 6–12 still wins for most hypertrophy work
summary: New lengthened-partial literature is exciting, but the practical coach takeaway remains: most weekly volume in a 6–12 (sometimes 5–15) zone with deep ranges of motion.
source: Simulated Habit Lab brief · ROM & rep-zone review

proposedChange.to: Bias accessories to 8–12; keep strength compounds at 4–8
proposedChange.explanation: We'll nudge accessory rep targets toward 8–12 while leaving main lifts in lower zones.

title: Deloods work better as planned volume cuts
summary: Athletes who planned a 40–50% volume deload every 4–6 weeks retained more strength than those who only deloaded reactively after joint niggles.
source: Simulated Habit Lab brief · periodization cohort

proposedChange.to: Keep weeks 4 & 8; treat them as ~60% volume, not total rest
proposedChange.explanation: Scheduled deloads stay — we emphasize skill practice over couch time.

title: Double progression still the simplest auto-regulator
summary: When lifters added load only after hitting the top of a rep range across all work sets, adherence and 12-week strength gains beat percentage-based weekly jumps for busy adults.
source: Simulated Habit Lab brief · progression RCT-style summary

proposedChange.to: Double progression: top of range on all sets → +2.5%
proposedChange.explanation: Confirms our default rule. No change needed unless you prefer weekly percentage jumps.

title: Sleep debt tanks next-session RPE more than missed macros
summary: In a monitored training group, <6 hours sleep predicted higher session RPE and fewer completed prescribed sets more strongly than a single high-carb or low-carb day.
source: Simulated Habit Lab brief · recovery monitoring

proposedChange.to: Prioritize sleep question in recovery audit
proposedChange.explanation: We'll highlight sleep in post-session check-ins before suggesting load cuts.

title: Protein ceiling myths vs. practical distribution
summary: For fat-loss phases, ~1.6–2.2 g/kg protein remains the evidence-backed band. Spreading across 3–4 meals beat a single mega-shake for lean-mass retention in dieting lifters.
source: Simulated Habit Lab brief · nutrition synthesis

proposedChange.to: Target ~1.8 g/kg across 3–4 feedings during fat loss
proposedChange.explanation: Dashboard nutrition tip updates; training volume stays put.

title: Minimum effective dose for maintenance is surprisingly low
summary: Trained adults maintained strength for 8–12 weeks on ~1/3 of prior weekly sets when intensity (proximity to failure) stayed high — useful for travel and crunch weeks.
source: Simulated Habit Lab brief · maintenance dose study

proposedChange.to: Offer a 1/3-volume maintenance mode for busy weeks
proposedChange.explanation: Coach Builder can propose a short maintenance template instead of skipping entirely.

title: Lengthened-bias accessories for stubborn muscles
summary: For lagging hamstrings and biceps, lengthened-position work (RDLs, incline curls) produced slightly better growth than shortened-only variants at matched effort.
source: Simulated Habit Lab brief · regional hypertrophy

proposedChange.to: Prefer lengthened-bias variations for weak points
proposedChange.explanation: When you flag hamstrings or biceps as a priority, we'll prefer RDL / incline-curl style options.

title: Cardio doesn't kill gains — timing might matter
summary: Concurrent training reviews show modest interference when hard intervals sit immediately before heavy lower-body strength. Separating by >6 hours or putting cardio after lifting blunted the effect.
source: Simulated Habit Lab brief · concurrent training

proposedChange.to: Prefer cardio after lifting or on separate days
proposedChange.explanation: We'll surface a timing tip when fat-loss users add conditioning.

title: Plateaus break faster with a stimulus change than more willpower
summary: Lifters stuck on a main lift for ≥2 weeks regained progress more often after a rep-zone or variation swap than after simply 'trying harder' at the same prescription.
source: Simulated Habit Lab brief · plateau interventions

proposedChange.to: Swap rep zone / variation before adding fatigue
proposedChange.explanation: Confirms our plateau rule: change the stimulus, don't just pile volume.
